doc.interviewee: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant

title: Bands in New Iberia: accordion, guitar and early brass bands
summary: He recalls accordion and guitar music, Bunk Johnson organizing a band, Saturday-night balls and quadrilles, and an accordionist named Lily.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: And what bands did you hear in New Iberia as you were growing up?

Well, in New Iberia at that time we had a band composed of the accordion. Oh, yeah. Mostly accordion music. That's the band there, accordion music and the guitar. Guitar and accordion. Yes. And finally we went on up to the halls, you know. Started to go in the halls. And Buck Johnson came in the band. He organized the band. Called Buck Johnson's band. So he started. And then he came in with the halls and the sliding tramboles and the brass band. That was after accordion and the guitar. And we had balls after balls. Every Saturday night was a big ball. Every Saturday night. That was a ball night. So we enjoyed that. That's why the quadrille really was ball out there. That was a quadrille every Saturday night.
What about those accordion players and guitar players? Do you remember any of their names?
Yeah, I know one player's name. A fellow used to be a professional at an accordion. His name was Lily.

Lily. His name was Lily. Do you remember bands from neighboring cities like, say, E. Van Thomas from Outta Crowley? Did you ever hear him? No, I don't remember. I just wondered if you'd ever heard of him. Mostly Bunk you remember.
